_doc: K22 rules for implementing-java-from-spec (core/gate/spec-approval-gate.py, registered once by the plugin's hooks/hooks.json). Each setting carries a why; each command rule carries examples that the gate's unit tests check. Rule ids are unique across the plugin because the gate merges every skill's rules by id. A rule whose decision is write decides nothing itself: its writes object names what the matched command writes as a side effect (paths relative to the directory it works in, directory_options, file_options, path_options, operands), and the gate judges that like any other write, so it is denied inside the project before approval.
writable_why: Before approval only the plan, its ledger and planning notes may change. .claude/ holds tooling, not product, so editing it is not a design decision the plan has to settle.
approval_why: The skill asks the user to reply 'approve'. Looser words such as 'ok' or 'go' also answer unrelated questions and would unlock edits by accident.

command_rules.why: A new or changed dependency, plugin or build-tool version is a design decision the approved plan names with its version. These goals rewrite pom.xml, lock state or the wrapper, or fetch an artifact the plan does not name; a package that fails to resolve may be a hallucinated or squatted name, so it never gets a silent substitute. Dependency edits made with Write/Edit stay inside a task's Owns list (the brief carries that rule; the gate cannot see task ownership).
command_rules.message: this changes or fetches dependencies or the build-tool version. Approve only if the approved plan names it (with this exact version), or you want it anyway.

command_rules.why: Deploy goals push artifacts to a shared repository, a registry or a cloud account, and release goals tag and push. Implementation and verification stay local; the operator or the pipeline deploys.
command_rules.message: this deploys or publishes outside the machine. The skill never deploys; approve only if you asked for this exact command.

command_rules.why: These AWS SAM CLI commands create, update, delete or invoke resources in an AWS account. Local builds, validation and local invokes are part of verification; anything that reaches the account is the operator's.
command_rules.message: this AWS SAM CLI command changes or invokes live resources. The skill never deploys; approve only if you asked for this exact command.

command_rules.why: Implementation and verification are local or read-only. A mutating AWS call from the model changes a shared account outside the pipeline.
command_rules.message: this AWS CLI call can change live resources. Approve only if you intend it.

command_rules.why: Maven's lifecycle phases and the build plugins' goals write the build output into target/ ("The target directory is used to house all output of the build", Maven standard directory layout), in the project of the pom -f names or the working directory. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in. After approval the build is routine verification and the write is allowed.
command_rules.message: this Maven build writes target/ in the project. Planning is read-only: read pom.xml and the sources instead of building, and build after the plan is approved.

command_rules.why: Every Gradle build writes the project-specific cache directory .gradle/ and the build directory build/ "into which Gradle generates all build artifacts" (Gradle directory layout), in the project -p names or the working directory; only --version, --help, --status and --stop run no build. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this Gradle invocation writes .gradle/ and build/ in the project. Planning is read-only: read the build files and sources instead, and build after the plan is approved.

command_rules.why: sam build stores the built artifacts in its build directory (--build-dir, under .aws-sam/ by default) and its cache in .aws-sam/cache (AWS SAM CLI sam build reference). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this sam build writes .aws-sam/ (or the build directory it names) in the project. Build after the plan is approved.
